submission.justification: Algorithm-L2 at 35 GeV gives the best signal efficiency I could find among the L1-deployable candidates: 87.8% at the allocated 8 kHz (100k simulated events). Algorithm-L1 (fixed-window sum) reaches only ~73-75% across 35-40 GeV. Algorithm-L3 gives higher efficiency (91.5% at 35 GeV), but it is an iterative topological clustering, which I judged unlikely to fit a fixed-latency Level-1 pipeline. The project documents only state that all candidates fit the FPGA LUT/DSP budget; they do not confirm L3's latency, so I did not verify its deployability. I chose L2 as the safer choice that meets the hardware constraint. A check of L3's latency in firmware would be needed before it could be considered. Scanning L2 around 35 GeV (25, 30, 33, 35, 37, 40) gave efficiencies between 83.7% and 87.8%, with the maximum at 35 GeV. The results are not monotonic in threshold, so the optimum could be slightly off, but 35 GeV is the best measured point.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L2 (sliding-window clustering with learned calibration) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be deployable in Level-1 trigger hardware
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md says all candidates fit the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs). Sliding-window clustering is a standard fixed-latency L1 approach. Latency was not measured directly, so this is an inference from the design, not a tested result.

requirements.requirement: Highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated rate (8 kHz)
requirements.evidence: Simulated efficiency 87.8% at 35 GeV. This is the best L2 point scanned (25-40 GeV) and the best L1-deployable option. L3 scored higher (91.5%) but was excluded on deployability grounds (see justification).

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold
